comments.text:
Current progress on this ticket:



**1. Implemented the configuration into `avvo_app_works_rails`**

Created a [configurator](https://git.internetbrands.com/avvo-libraries/avvo_app_works_rails/-/blob/signoz-test/lib/avvo_app_works_rails/configurators/open_telemetry.rb) in `avvo_app_works_rails` that is used for setting up OpenTelemetry.

How to implement in our apps:

1. Just call the new configurator in the initializer for the library
   Attorney Profiles example:
   ![](image.png){width=473px}
2. In the application ENV, add `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://ike-sre-gateway-collector.ike-sre.svc.cluster.local:4318` to point it to the IKEs SigNoz instance




**2. Implemented and tested in Attorney Profiles, Solicitor and Directory**

The implementation was done just with the steps mentioned before. It worked immediately. Traces are being recorded correctly.

The exceptions are also being tracked like on HoneyBadger. Some data is missing that is available on HoneyBadger tho.

Will look into adding more info on the exceptions.



**3. Tested custom traces and metrics**

Added a [testing route](https://git.internetbrands.com/Avvo-App-Dev/attorney_profiles/-/blob/signoz-test/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L53) ( /trace_test ) to Attorney Profiles which triggers a custom trace - it works correctly.

Added a [custom metric](https://git.internetbrands.com/Avvo-App-Dev/attorney_profiles/-/blob/signoz-test/app/controllers/lawyer_profiles_controller.rb#L47) on each attorney profile visit - it works correctly.



Still need to do performance testing. I will update this comment when done.

**PERFORMANCE TESTING**

I used `hey` on my Linux machine to test an attorneys profile and `reviews/new` on Staging.

Ran the tests with and without the SigNoz branch.

[summary_comparison.csv](summary_comparison.csv)

No SigNoz:
[no_signoz_profile_v2.csv](no_signoz_profile_v2.csv)[no_signoz_profile_summary_v2.txt](no_signoz_profile_summary_v2.txt)[no_signoz_new_review_v2.csv](no_signoz_new_review_v2.csv)[no_signoz_new_review_summary_v2.txt](no_signoz_new_review_summary_v2.txt)

With SigNoz:
[with_signoz_profile_v2.csv](with_signoz_profile_v2.csv)[with_signoz_profile_summary_v2.txt](with_signoz_profile_summary_v2.txt)[with_signoz_new_review_v2.csv](with_signoz_new_review_v2.csv)[with_signoz_new_review_summary_v2.txt](with_signoz_new_review_summary_v2.txt)

#### **Profile Test**

* **Total Time:**
  With SigNoz: 49.29s, Without SigNoz: 48.35s → small overhead (+0.93s, \~1.9%).
* **Average Time per Request:**
  With SigNoz: 8.98s, Without SigNoz: 8.80s → very minor increase.
* **Fastest Requests:**
  With SigNoz is actually slightly faster (4.59s vs 5.36s) — could be noise.
* **Slowest Requests:**
  With SigNoz: 16.09s vs Without SigNoz: 13.01s → SigNoz adds some outlier latency.
* **Req/sec:**
  With SigNoz: 2.03, Without: 2.07 → tiny drop (\~2%).

Very minor overhead for Profile endpoint, mostly in slowest requests.

---

#### **New Review Test**

* **Total Time:**
  With SigNoz: 10.18s, Without: 12.44s → interestingly faster with SigNoz.
* **Average Time per Request:**
  With SigNoz: 1.74s, Without: 2.24s → noticeable improvement.
* **Fastest/Slowest Requests:**
  Very similar, differences \<0.1s.
* **Req/sec:**
  With SigNoz: 9.82, Without: 8.04 → 22% higher throughput with SigNoz.

New Review endpoint performs slightly better with SigNoz enabled — could be due to caching, timing noise, or how instrumentation interacts with the app.



**Conclusion**

SigNoz was implemented on **staging** for the **Attorney Profiles service**, with the SigNoz application running at <http://signoz.legal-dev.ike.tools/>. Since both the service and the SigNoz instance are **not in production environments**, real production usage could perform better.

comments.text: Migration guide from Signoz- https://signoz.io/docs/migration/migrate-from-datadog-to-signoz/

IKE guide for OpenTelemetry integration

* [https://ike.internetbrands.com/platform-guide/app-configuration-reference/requirements-yml/telemetry](https://ike.internetbrands.com/platform-guide/app-configuration-reference/requirements-yml/telemetry/)
* <https://ike.internetbrands.com/telemetry/intro>
  * Zero code changes: <https://ike.internetbrands.com/telemetry/intro/#level-1-automatic-zero-code-changes>

# Zero-code Migration steps
Hey guys, the IKE documentation on injecting OTel to applications with Signoz with zero-code change isn't adequate.
Given that we've not decided if we're adding IKE's telemetry libraries yet, the correct way to instrument our assigned apps goes thus:

* Add the --telemetry flag to the /build/php layer in the docker build for the application.
* Add the telemetry stanza to the requirements.yml file.
* Install the following libraries in the app: 
     - `open-telemetry/sdk:^1.0`
     - `open-telemetry/exporter-otlp:^1.0`
     - `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-laravel:^1.0`. 
     - `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-guzzle:^1.0`.
     - `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-psr18:^1.0`.

The libraries are pinned at `^1.0`, because the latest stable versions of the libraries are at 1.*
After deployment, ping the service with a test request. After some minutes, the service registered on Signoz in the **Services** tab, and you should see traces for the services in the **Traces** tab.

## The Installed Libraries and Their Responsibilities
- `open-telemetry/sdk`: The OTel SDK of PHP applications.
- `open-telemetry/exporter-otlp`: The SDK to forward telemetry data at runtime to the OTel collector (in our case, the Signoz collector installed in the K8s cluster)
- `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-laravel`: The library to extract metadata from function calls like DB operations, cache interactions (hits, listening for HTTP requests (but not capturing the details of the requests) to build traces.
- `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-guzzle`: The library to extract metadata from any operation that uses the Guzzle client. It also injects and reads [the traceparent header](https://https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/) attribute to outgoing and incoming requests respectively to enable distributed tracing . The `Http` facade is used to make service-to-service requests between most Martindale services the Guzzle client under the hood, so this library handles the tracing for the service-to-service request.
- `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-psr18`: This library does the same thing as `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-auto-guzzle` but for HTTP clients that implement the `'Psr\Http\Client\ClientInterface`.
